# markdown-s2 — Safe Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S2) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown: string, { headingIds = false } = {}): string` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown: string): Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>` — every ATX/setext heading in document order; `text` is the heading's plain text (inline markup removed). - `export function slugify(text: string, seen?: Map)` — GitHub-style slug: lower-case; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`; spaces → `-`. When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags is not significant to the tests; `
`/`

My title

`. - Paragraphs; soft line breaks preserved as `\n`; hard breaks via two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash → `
`. - Emphasis/strong with `*` and `_` (CommonMark rules incl. no intraword `_` emphasis), `***x***` → `x`; GFM `~~strike~~` → ``. - Code spans (multi-backtick delimiters, one leading/trailing space stripped when both present). - Fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, info string → `class="language-"`) and indented code blocks. - Blockquotes (nested, with lazy continuation lines), thematic breaks (`---`, `***`, `___`). - Bullet lists (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered lists (`1.` / `1)`, `start` attribute when not 1), nesting by indentation, tight vs loose lists (`

content.text: All outputs match CommonMark/GFM. Adding a test file and checking the CLI.

I built the Markdown → HTML renderer described in SPEC.md, entirely from my own code. `node --test` passes all 9 tests: the 2 public smoke tests and 7 of my own.

**`src/markdown.js`** exports `render`, `toc` and `slugify`.
- **Structure:** it follows the same design as the CommonMark reference implementation: lines are first grouped into blocks, then the text inside each block is parsed for emphasis, links and so on.
- **Block features:** both heading styles, paragraphs, hard and soft line breaks, fenced and indented code blocks (with `language-…` classes), nested blockquotes with lazy continuation lines, thematic breaks, and bullet and ordered lists. Lists support nesting, tight vs. loose output and the `start` attribute.
- **Inline features:** emphasis and strong (following the CommonMark rules), `~~strike~~` → `<del>`, code spans, inline and reference links and images, autolinks (email ones become `mailto:`), backslash escapes and HTML entities. Only a common subset of named entities is recognised, in `src/entities.js`; any other named entity is printed as literal text.
- **GFM tables:** alignment, inline markup in cells, `\|` escapes, padding or cutting body rows to the header's cell count, and a table that starts right after paragraph text.
- **Safety:**
  - Raw HTML, both block and inline, is always shown as escaped text.
  - Link and image URLs using `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` become `#`. The only exception is `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`.
  - The check is done after decoding and ignores case and whitespace, so `JAVASCRIPT:` is also caught.
- **Heading IDs and TOC:** slugs follow GitHub's style, and repeated headings get `-1`, `-2`, … using one map per document. This is used by both `headingIds` and `toc()`.

**`src/cli.js`** runs as `node src/cli.js <file|-> [--toc] [--ids]` and reads stdin when given `-`.

Beyond the tests, I checked the output by hand against CommonMark behaviour I know (emphasis rules, link edge cases, lazy lines, tabs). That's only as reliable as my memory of the spec, since this condition doesn't allow fetching the official spec examples.

My tests are in `tests/unit/markdown.test.js`. `PROVENANCE.json` stays `[]` because nothing external was reused.
